content: Magnesium-based treatments are utilized to address various complications in individuals suffering from chronic kidney disease (CKD). These interventions often aim to manage magnesium imbalances, which are common in CKD patients due to impaired kidney function. Magnesium plays a critical role in numerous physiological processes, including neuromuscular function, cardiovascular health, and bone metabolism. In CKD, both hypermagnesemia (elevated magnesium levels) and hypomagnesemia (low magnesium levels) can occur, each associated with distinct clinical risks. Magnesium supplementation may be considered in cases of hypomagnesemia to restore normal levels and mitigate associated symptoms, such as muscle cramps, arrhythmias, or fatigue. Conversely, in patients with hypermagnesemia, strategies to reduce magnesium levels may involve dietary restrictions, adjustments in magnesium-containing medications, or dialysis in severe cases. Additionally, magnesium-based phosphate binders are sometimes prescribed to CKD patients to control hyperphosphatemia, a common complication that contributes to vascular calcification and cardiovascular disease. These binders help reduce phosphate absorption in the gastrointestinal tract while potentially offering the added benefit of improving magnesium balance. The use of magnesium-based interventions requires careful monitoring of serum magnesium levels, as well as consideration of the patient’s overall clinical status, including kidney function, cardiovascular health, and concurrent medications. Balancing magnesium levels is essential to minimize risks and optimize outcomes in CKD management.
